text:
maria: Heads up — did a helm upgrade for "runtime-release" to v2.4.1 and it ended up in pending-upgrade. Looks like the post-upgrade job is Pending and helm timed out. deploy-bot: `upgrade runtime-release v2.4.1 failed: timed out waiting for post-upgrade job`
ken: can you paste the pod status?
maria: kubectl get pods -n infra-system runtime-post-job-7d8f Pending

maria: kubectl describe pod runtime-post-job-7d8f -n infra-system shows:
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age                From               Message
  ----     ------             ----               ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled          5m                 default-scheduler  pod did not match node selector
  Warning  FailedScheduling   5m (x3 over 5m)    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 node(s) didn't match node selector.

maria: job template uses nodeSelector: `gpu: nvidia` but our autoscaler/terraform rollout renamed label to `gpu.vendor: nvidia` last night (drift).
anish: ahhh that'd do it — when the job has a strict nodeSelector it's impossible for it to schedule if labels changed. Terraform change was applied by autoscaler change PR?
ken: yep we had a cloud autoscaler update that normalized node labels, forgot to update infra jobs.

sre-oncall: note: helm is holding the release in pending-upgrade state until the Job completes. That blocks future automated rollouts for this chart. Flux-bot: flux will keep reconciling the Git repo and may try to reapply the same chart which won't help while helm is stuck.

maria: quick plan: (1) pause flux for this namespace, (2) patch job template to accept both selectors, (3) run `helm upgrade --reuse-values` to re-run hooks, (4) after completion unpause flux. Thoughts?
ken: sounds good. For safety I'd avoid deleting the release. If step 2 is small, we can manually patch the Job in-cluster to get it to run now: `kubectl patch job runtime-post-job-7d8f -n infra-system --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector/gpu"}]'` — that should let it schedule (assuming tolerations ok). After it's done we can update chart and commit.
anish: and make sure we update Terraform module to keep consistent label keys. I'll open a rollback/patch PR to restore the old label alias until charts are updated.
sre-oncall: FYI if you need to clear the helm lock quicker: `helm uninstall runtime-release --keep-history` will remove the release resources but keep history; but that is disruptive. Prefer patching the job first.

maria: ok doing step 1: pausing flux for infra-system. flux-bot: `suspend: true` applied to Kustomization infra-system (paused).
ken: after that you can patch the job. Watch for nodeAffinity as well — we've seen some jobs using preferredDuringScheduling that still fail.
maria: patched the job and it's scheduling now. Pod started pulling image.

maria: helm status now shows the post-upgrade hook completed and release moved to deployed. Good.
anish: follow-up: open PR to update chart's job to use flexible nodeSelector (accept both `gpu` and `gpu.vendor`) + add a readiness probe so long-running jobs report progress in logs.

sre-oncall: also add a CI lint that checks job scheduling against current node labels in staging to catch this earlier.
ken: +1. I'll also add a note to the runbook about pausing GitOps before manual fixes to avoid reconcile fights.

maria: tl;dr — root cause = label drift from a terraform/autoscaler change causing post-upgrade hook Job to be unschedulable, helm waited and left release pending. Fix = pause flux, patch job to allow scheduling, confirm hook completes, then update chart + terraform to converge.
deploy-bot: Closed alert #INF-3421 (helm job stuck)
flux-bot: Kustomization infra-system remains paused.
